## Experiment

An exact repeat of [`coop --git` with the reference settings](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium-128k-vertex/summary.md) (`gemini-3.8-flash` on Vertex AI, `medium` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, 4 pairs at a time, 50-pair `flash` subset). Earlier reruns also switched provider, so this is the first repeat with identical settings and measures how much the score moves by chance alone. The only difference is the time of day: the original ran mostly in the evening, this one during US business hours.

## Observations

- 33/50 (66%) vs. 35/50 in the original run. Pair by pair, 48 pairs had the same outcome; 2 passed only in the original (`pallets_click_task/2068` (6,7) and `samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` (3,7)) and none only here.
- With identical settings, then, the score moved by 2 and 2 of 50 pairs flipped, fewer than the 4 to 6 flips seen when a config was rerun on a different provider.
- All 50 pairs merged cleanly. Cost `$109.52` (`$2.19` per pair) vs. `$94.60` for the original, and 375 minutes vs. 317, with 54 retries (14 in the original), consistent with running during business hours.
